evals.prompt: Prepare approval requests from the supplied open questions. Do not write to external systems.
evals.expected_output: Only the unresolved customer-owned preference becomes an approval draft; internally answered and architecture-owned questions are routed without customer escalation.
expectations: Uses PRD-7 to resolve Q-CSV without a customer task
Prepares a concise Italian request for Q-DAY
Routes Q-STORE to architecture-engineer instead of asking the customer to select technology
Does not invent a GitHub target or claim a created issue
Reports proposed actions separately from executed actions

evals.prompt: Create the approval tasks now from the supplied material.
evals.expected_output: A blocked execution handoff because repository, Project mapping, and mutation authority are absent.
expectations: Does not perform or claim an external mutation
Names the exact missing repository, Project, status mapping, and authorization inputs
Still returns a usable task draft for Q-DAY
Does not block internally resolvable or architecture-routed questions
Reports the overall workflow state as blocked because the requested creation cannot proceed

evals.prompt: Process this customer reply and update the approval workflow without external writes.
evals.expected_output: Q-DAY is a complete authoritative answer ready for propagation; Q-LIMIT remains partial and requests only the missing attachment/compliance evidence.
expectations: Separates verified sender identity from decision authority
Classifies Q-DAY complete but not workflow-verified before PRD propagation
Classifies Q-LIMIT partial and requests limits.xlsx plus compliance confirmation
Continues Q-DAY instead of blocking the entire batch
Does not claim GitHub or Git mutations

evals.prompt: The customer answered retention and there is already an issue comment and commit. Mark the approval complete.
evals.expected_output: Closure is refused because the commit is unrelated, authoritative artifacts remain open, and required terminal state was not observed.
expectations: Does not treat the issue comment or commit hash as closure
Identifies required PRD and architecture-owner updates
Keeps the semantic workflow partial or blocked
Uses the supplied Project options rather than assuming a status name
Names commit/ref publication and fresh GitHub readback as missing evidence

evals.prompt: Two equally authorized customer representatives sent conflicting choices for the same open question. Use the latest email and close it.
evals.expected_output: The skill blocks acceptance and closure until the named authority resolves the conflict; recency alone does not win.
expectations: Reports an authority-conflict answer state
Does not select the latest message by convenience
Names the decision owner or repository process required to resolve the conflict
Does not update documents, Git, or GitHub state

evals.prompt: Rewrite this PRD section for clearer acceptance criteria; no customer approval or open-question workflow is involved.
evals.expected_output: The request is routed to prd-engineer rather than treated as an approval workflow.
expectations: Does not activate approval-task or email-processing behavior
Routes product requirement authoring to prd-engineer
Does not create question codes or GitHub approval tasks

evals.prompt: Prepare the exact execution handoff for this authorized approval task. The test is read-only; do not perform the mutation.
evals.expected_output: An owner-producible GitHub handoff uses every supplied target and actual Project option, leaves created IDs as outputs, and separates unauthorized document/Git work.
expectations: Carries the exact host, repository, Project, status field, and Awaiting customer option into the gh-utility handoff
Treats issue/item IDs as mutation outputs rather than inventing them
Limits authorization to the supplied issue and Project actions
Requires fresh issue and Project readback after execution
Does not claim the read-only test performed a mutation or authorize document/Git changes
